picks.file: Beschreibung der Städt der Welt - Braun & Hogenberg - btv1b52512111k (083 of 378).jpg
picks.what: View across the Weser, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored copy (German edition) of the 1572 plate; trimmed to the ‘Brema’ panel from the four-city sheet; church spires, ships and the Weser bridge

picks.file: Gezicht op de markt te Bremen, RP-P-2018-1316.jpg
picks.what: The market square with the town hall, the Roland and the Schütting, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Saxoniae Inferioris (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: the city’s best-known scene; cleaner and larger than the book scan #11; legend and margins cut

picks.what: View across the Weser with the Great Weser Bridge, colored engraving in Bechstein’s Album der Haupt- und Residenzstädte Europa’s
picks.why: colored general view of the old town’s river front and church towers; title cut

picks.what: The cathedral seen from Kaiser-Wilhelm-Platz, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color view of the cathedral’s twin spires behind the town hall; border and caption cut

gaps: P0: no candidates; P5: nothing good; P6: nothing usable
notes: #31 is Bremerhaven, a different city. P5 options left out: #29 (1965 color slide across the Weser, cathedral spires tiny, barbed wire in front) and #28 (port aerial dated only 1955–65). P6 candidates are only flood and port aerials. Skipped #19 (1818 journeyman’s certificate: skyline strip under text, likely copied from an older plate) and #15/#16 (dated only 1800–1899). #2 is a later B&H plan in a tightly bound book.
